audit_findings.title: Every scenario perpetuates a record-high earnings level
audit_findings.magnitude: The $54.0 million anchor is $12.0 million above 2024 OE and $18.3 million above 2023 OE; the latest nine-month filing also reports Business-to-Business operating income down $6.422 million, or 14%
audit_findings.mechanism: The peak enters every forecast as starting OE and is also capitalized through a terminal value representing 47.7%-51.5% of operating PV
audit_findings.evidence: Oil-Dri experienced another record-breaking year with consolidated net sales, gross profit and net income reaching all-time highs.
audit_findings.explanation: The peak anchor and absence of a below-anchor bear case are demonstrated. A future decline is not demonstrated, but recent weakness in fluids purification and margins makes level normalization reasonably capable of materially reducing all scenarios.
audit_findings.action: Build a mid-cycle OE excluding temporary demand, mix and acquisition effects, add scenarios beginning below $54.0 million, and rerun the full DCF and terminal value.

audit_findings.title: Growth may be credited without all required reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 capital expenditure of $32.562 million exceeded depreciation and amortization of $22.042 million by $10.520 million; at 26.1% RONTA, first-year reinvestment implied by 3% and 6% growth is approximately $6.2 million and $12.4 million
audit_findings.mechanism: If growth reinvestment is omitted, forecast OE is overstated by the capital required to produce incremental earnings
audit_findings.evidence: Cash used in investing activities primarily related to capital expenditures to expand our plant equipment and improve our facilities in order to support increased demand for our products.
audit_findings.explanation: The elevated investment spending is demonstrated, but the supplied valuation record does not establish whether scenario cash flows deduct growth reinvestment. The computed requirement is 11.5%-23.0% of the $54.0 million anchor in the first year and is therefore potentially material.
audit_findings.action: Produce the forecast cash-flow formulas showing maintenance capex and growth reinvestment separately; if reinvestment is absent, deduct growth divided by 26.1% RONTA each year and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The later cash bridge may overlap the forecast period
audit_findings.magnitude: Cash increased $12.483 million between July 31, 2025 and April 30, 2026, equal to approximately $0.86 per share; the duplicated portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-FY2025 cash generation can enter both April 2026 bridge cash and a forecast period beginning from FY2025
audit_findings.evidence: Cash and cash equivalents, including restricted cash, totaled $50.5 million and $24.5 million as of July 31, 2025, and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed valuation dates are demonstrated, but the first forecast date and discount timing are not supplied. Consequently, the record cannot establish whether double counting occurred or how much of the $12.483 million cash increase overlaps forecast OE.
audit_findings.action: Document the valuation date, first forecast cash-flow date and discount periods; prepare a July 2025-to-April 2026 stub roll-forward and include each stub cash flow either in bridge cash or operating PV, but not both.

audit_findings.title: The denominator assumes equal economics across two unequal classes
audit_findings.magnitude: Using the filed 133.33% participation ratio and April 2026 outstanding shares produces indicated Common values of approximately $52.49, $61.20 and $71.33 versus reported bear, base and bull values of $48.68, $56.71 and $66.13; maximum difference approximately $5.20 per Common share
audit_findings.mechanism: An unweighted aggregate denominator allocates equal OE to Common and Class B shares despite Common's greater economic participation
audit_findings.evidence: Common Stock is entitled to cash dividends equal to at least 133.33 % on a per share basis of the cash dividend paid on Class B Stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The unequal rights are demonstrated. A two-class allocation would increase the publicly traded Common valuation, but even the computed bull value of about $71.33 remains $16.57 below the $87.90 valuation-date price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: State explicitly whether the result assumes full conversion; otherwise apply the filing's two-class allocation to OE and bridge value and report Common and Class B values separately.

audit_findings.title: The anchor includes a nonrecurring tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: The filed prior-year tax adjustment reduced the effective rate by 1.7 percentage points, approximately $1.126 million on $66.211 million of pretax income; a proportional DCF sensitivity is approximately $0.94-$1.29 per share across scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: The one-time tax benefit increases anchor OE and is capitalized through forecast earnings and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: Favorable return to provision adjustments for returns filed in 2025 drove a decrease in the 2025 effective tax rate.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization item. Its computed effect is only about 2.1% of the $54.0 million anchor and cannot close the $21.77 gap between the $66.13 bull value and the $87.90 price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the return-to-provision reconciliation, subtract the approximately $1.126 million benefit from anchor OE, apply a sustainable tax rate, and rerun the scenarios as a normalization check.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance is treated as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: The maximum bridge exposure is the full $62.941 million, or approximately $4.34 per share, representing 6.6% of bull equity value and less than the $21.77 gap between bull value and market price
audit_findings.mechanism: Any operating cash incorrectly classified as surplus is added directly to equity value through the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: Our principal liquidity needs are to fund our capital requirements, including funding working capital needs; purchasing and upgrading equipment, facilities, information systems, and real estate; supporting new product development; investing in infrastructure; repurchasing stock; paying dividends; and, from time to time, business acquisitions and funding our debt service requirements.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate that all cash is surplus, but the full balance provides a conservative upper bound on this bridge issue. Even removing all $62.941 million would reduce the bull value to about $61.79 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion at $87.90.
audit_findings.action: Calculate minimum operating cash from monthly working-capital seasonality, payroll, debt service and committed capital spending, then add only the documented surplus in the bridge.
